title: Adaptive Kernel Learning via Evolutionary Differential Programming
abstract: Kernel learning remains a central challenge in machine learning, largely due to the difficulty in selecting an appropriate kernel function and its associated parameters. Traditional methods frequently rely on subjective heuristics, leading to suboptimal performance and limited adaptability to diverse datasets. This work introduces a novel approach, Adaptive Kernel Learning via Evolutionary Differential Programming, which addresses this issue by integrating evolutionary optimization with differential programming. The core idea is to simultaneously learn the kernel function and its parameters using an evolutionary algorithm, allowing the system to dynamically adapt to the underlying data distribution. The algorithm utilizes differential programming to guide the evolutionary search, ensuring convergence towards solutions that maximize both prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. The system's adaptive nature eliminates the need for manual tuning and possesses the potential to discover superior kernels compared to conventional methods. The presented framework offers a fully automated and robust solution for kernel selection, paving the way for improved machine learning performance across a broad range of applications.

title: Adaptive Geometry in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive geometry in neural networks to enhance learning and generalization. We introduce a novel mechanism that dynamically adjusts the geometry of internal representations based on the data being processed, fostering a more robust and adaptable model. The core claim is that this adaptive geometry approach can significantly improve performance across a range of tasks, addressing a fundamental challenge in deep learning. This work presents a theoretical framework and demonstrates the efficacy of this mechanism through simulation and preliminary experimentation.

title: Quantum Bioinformatics
abstract: This paper explores the emerging field of quantum bioinformatics, proposing a novel approach to tackling complex challenges within biological information analysis. Traditional biological data processing often encounters limitations due to the exponential growth of datasets and the computational intensity of tasks like sequence alignment, gene prediction, and protein structure prediction. We posit that quantum computing, leveraging phenomena like superposition and entanglement, offers a paradigm shift capable of dramatically accelerating these calculations. This document details the core concept of representing biological sequences as quantum states and utilizing quantum algorithms – specifically tailored for bioinformatics applications – to perform these computations. The theoretical framework incorporates key quantum principles to enhance efficiency and potentially unlock new insights in biological systems. We present a foundational model for quantum sequence alignment, quantum gene prediction, and quantum protein structure prediction, outlining the mathematical formulations and algorithmic approaches. The potential impact of this work is significant, suggesting a future where quantum bioinformatics becomes a cornerstone of biological research. ---

title: Beyond Classification: Structured Supervision Aligns Visual Evidence with Medical Semantics
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have shown immense potential in medical image analysis. However, standard pre-training via global image classification suffers from spatial collapse, where models rely heavily on background shortcuts rather than localising critical foreground lesions. To overcome this limitation and align visual evidence with precise medical semantics, we systematically investigate alternative pre-training paradigms.Specifically, we evaluate three independent forms of structured supervision: topological priors via graph self-supervision, dense pixel-level constraints via segmentation, and cross-modal semantic grounding via image-text pairs. Notably, our empirical analysis reveals that while all three forms of structured supervision successfully alleviate the global pooling bottleneck and steer visual attention towards foreground regions, image-text alignment achieves the most superior performance. By embedding high-dimensional diagnostic logic, the cross-modal approach not only anchors attention on precise visual evidence but also enables profound abstract reasoning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this semantically enriched pre-training fundamentally enhances the model's feature representation. Consequently, when fine-tuned for downstream clinical classification tasks, our models achieve superior accuracy and yield highly interpretable attention maps focused on true pathological features, vastly outperforming vanilla classification baselines.

title: Digital Preservation of Rhodope Dialects Through Intelligent Language Technologies
abstract: The article presents a prototype intelligent language modelling system to preserve Rhodope dialects. Implemented in Prolog, it converts dialectal into standard Bulgarian lexical units and vice versa, generating the corresponding grammatical form. It includes a module for phonetic features and demonstrates the application of symbolic AI in digital cultural heritage.

title: Dynamically Adaptive Neural Architecture Search via Evolutionary Strategies
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Neural Architecture Search (NAS) that leverages Evolutionary Strategies (ES) with dynamic adaptation. Traditional NAS methods often suffer from high computational cost and the tendency to converge to suboptimal architectures. Our proposed system addresses these limitations by creating a self-optimizing NAS framework where the ES algorithm itself adjusts its search parameters – specifically mutation and crossover rates – based on the performance of the architectures it generates. This dynamic adaptation, facilitated by a learning rate adaptation module, allows the ES to efficiently explore the architecture search space and ultimately discover more effective architectures. We demonstrate that this dynamically adaptive ES-based NAS method significantly outperforms static ES approaches and often converges to superior architectures with reduced computational expense. The core of our method lies in the continuous feedback loop between architecture performance and the evolutionary strategy's parameters, leading to a more refined and targeted search. The system provides a practical and efficient solution for NAS, especially in scenarios with limited computational resources.

title: ##基于拓扑保护的深度神经网络训练
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to training deep neural networks by leveraging topological protection. Traditional deep learning training suffers from instability issues like vanishing and exploding gradients, leading to slow convergence and difficulties in achieving optimal performance. Our method introduces topological constraints within the network's connection weight matrices, effectively creating a topologically protected environment. This protection mitigates gradient instability, accelerates convergence, and ultimately improves the training stability of deep neural networks. We demonstrate the efficacy of this technique through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework. The core claim of this work is that utilizing the inherent topological structure of neural networks through a protection mechanism significantly enhances training stability and accelerates convergence speed. This work represents a new methodology for training deep networks, moving beyond purely gradient-based approaches and incorporating principles from topology. ---

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Curriculum Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that integrates hierarchical reinforcement learning, intrinsic motivation, and curriculum learning. The core idea is to create a multi-level agent capable of both strategic planning (high-level) and detailed execution (low-level), guided by an internal drive for exploration (intrinsic motivation) and a structured learning progression (curriculum learning). We demonstrate that carefully orchestrating these elements can significantly improve the training efficiency and performance of complex RL agents. The framework dynamically adapts the learning environment based on the agent's capabilities, fostering more effective learning compared to traditional RL methods. This work offers a promising direction for tackling challenging RL problems where defining appropriate reward functions and designing suitable environments can be difficult.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Based on Biological Neuron Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of biological neuron models to enhance multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithms. Traditional MARL approaches often struggle with scalability, robustness, and efficient learning, particularly in complex environments. This research proposes a novel framework that leverages the inherent characteristics of biological neurons – including time constants, thresholds, and synaptic plasticity – to create more effective and biologically inspired multi-agent systems. The core idea is to model individual agents as networks of interconnected neurons, employing these models to capture the dynamic behavior of each agent. We formulate the MARL problem as a pulse emission problem within these neuron networks. This approach allows for the incorporation of biologically plausible learning mechanisms, potentially leading to improved agent performance and learning speed compared to purely artificial neural network-based MARL solutions. The study focuses on designing and evaluating algorithms that utilize these biological neuron models in conjunction with established reinforcement learning techniques, demonstrating the potential for enhanced robustness and learning efficiency in multi-agent scenarios. The key contributions of this work are the integration of biophysical modeling into MARL and the demonstration of improved learning characteristics.

title: Dynamic Probabilistic Model Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to probabilistic model learning, termed Dynamic Probabilistic Model Learning (DPL). The core idea is to construct a model capable of real-time learning and adaptation to environmental changes, utilizing this model for decision-making and control, thereby enhancing system robustness and adaptability. Traditional probabilistic model learning methods often suffer from a static nature, rendering them ineffective when faced with dynamic environments. DPL addresses this limitation by incorporating a dynamic update mechanism, enabling the probability model to continuously refine and optimize itself based on environmental feedback. The proposed framework is rooted in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), but expands upon them with a mechanism for ongoing probabilistic model evolution. This allows the system to respond effectively to unforeseen shifts in the environment, significantly improving performance compared to static models. We outline the key components of the DPL framework, focusing on the dynamic updating process and its implications for decision-control strategies. The theoretical foundations and the overall approach are presented, laying the groundwork for future research and implementation.

title: Bias-Driven Quantum Decoherence Control
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to mitigating decoherence in quantum systems – bias-driven quantum decoherence control. The core concept revolves around introducing artificial biases, specifically through precisely controlled microwave or optical fields, to selectively suppress detrimental decoherence pathways. Traditional decoherence suppression techniques often introduce systematic errors. We demonstrate that by strategically applying these biases, we can significantly enhance the coherence time of target quantum states. The theoretical framework outlines the key principles and mathematical formulations underlying this approach, focusing on the manipulation of the decoherence rate and the resultant impact on quantum state fidelity. We present a model demonstrating how bias can effectively filter out unwanted decoherence events, leading to improved quantum computation accuracy and stability. The research highlights the potential of bias control as a robust and adaptable strategy for tackling the inherent challenges of quantum decoherence.

title: Non-Linear Topological Geometry Quantum State Dynamics
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear topological geometry as a foundation for quantum state dynamics simulations, with a focus on molecular physics and materials science. We propose a novel computational framework leveraging quantum entanglement and topological properties to model complex systems, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The core mechanism involves constructing a computational model that describes quantum state evolution through topological transformations, facilitated by quantum entanglement, leading to accelerated simulation capabilities. We address the challenge of accurately capturing quantum dynamics within these models, particularly in complex systems with intricate interactions. This work lays the groundwork for a new approach to simulating quantum systems, potentially offering improved fidelity and efficiency compared to traditional approaches.

title: Dynamic Topology Mapping – Based on Self-Organized Neural Networks for Geometric Deformation
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic topology mapping approach utilizing self-organized neural networks for geometric deformation. Traditional geometric transformation algorithms rely on predefined rules, limiting flexibility and efficiency. We introduce a novel module, the "Self-Organized Neural Network Geometry Deformation Module," that learns and applies geometric transformations through the inherent properties of self-organized networks. This module enables efficient and accurate dynamic reshaping of complex geometric shapes, offering a significant improvement over existing methods. The paper details the implementation of this module and demonstrates its effectiveness through several illustrative examples. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the network's ability to model and adapt to intricate transformations.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Complexity Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the computational complexity of quantum algorithms, proposing a new framework based on quantum superposition and entanglement. We introduce a "quantum state evolution" algorithm to dynamically adjust the quantum state, enabling the calculation of complexity metrics directly tied to the algorithm's objectives. The core claim is that this approach offers a fundamentally new method for quantifying the computational limits of quantum algorithms, surpassing current classical approximations. We provide a detailed mathematical description of the algorithm and discuss its implications for understanding and potentially extending the limits of quantum computation.

title: Dynamically Constructed Modular Proof Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for constructing mathematical proofs through a dynamically constructed modular framework. The core idea is to define a set of 'building blocks' representing fundamental mathematical concepts and then generate proofs by assembling these blocks in a way that leverages the problem's structure. We introduce a 'proof engine' that automatically adjusts building blocks based on the problem's characteristics, resulting in proofs that are more efficient and adaptable. The system's design addresses the limitations of traditional proof systems by offering greater flexibility and potentially enhanced computational efficiency. We explore the core mechanism, detailing the building block structure and the proof engine's operational logic. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for various mathematical domains.

title: Quantum Simulation of Phase Transitions with Adaptive Sampling
abstract: Simulating phase transitions using quantum computers presents a significant challenge due to the complex and often chaotic nature of these transitions. Traditional quantum simulation methods often rely on uniform sampling of the relevant phase space, leading to inefficient resource utilization and prohibitively long simulation times. This work proposes a novel approach to quantum simulation of phase transitions that leverages adaptive sampling, guided by reinforcement learning, to dynamically adjust the sampling strategy. The core idea is to identify and focus on regions of the phase space where the transition is most pronounced, thereby minimizing the overall computational cost. We formulate the problem as a Markov decision process, where the quantum computer's sampling strategy is the agent and the simulation's performance is the reward. Reinforcement learning algorithms are employed to train the agent, enabling it to learn an optimal sampling policy. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, the potential of this adaptive sampling method to significantly reduce the computational burden associated with simulating phase transitions while maintaining accuracy. Future work will involve exploring specific algorithms and architectures for implementing this approach on actual quantum hardware.

title: Title: Bayesian Stochastic Dynamics in Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian stochastic dynamics to modeling complex dynamical systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with the inherent uncertainty within these systems, limiting the precision of parameter estimation and hindering the ability to accurately predict future states. We propose a novel Bayesian framework that leverages prior distributions to guide parameter estimation, enabling more robust and adaptable modeling. This approach addresses key limitations in existing techniques, providing a principled and verifiable method for navigating the complexities of dynamical systems. The core mechanism involves replacing gradient-based optimization with Bayesian inference, incorporating a prior distribution on the model's parameters to provide a more stable and reliable estimate of the system's evolution. This paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis and illustrative examples demonstrating the efficacy of this Bayesian framework.

title: Graph-Based Representation Learning for Explainable AI
abstract: The increasing deployment of complex AI models, particularly deep neural networks, has raised significant concerns regarding their lack of explainability. Understanding *why* a model makes a specific prediction is crucial for trust, debugging, and regulatory compliance. This research proposes a novel approach to enhance AI explainability by leveraging graph-based representation learning. We construct a graph that explicitly represents the relationships between input features and the internal variables within a neural network. This graph allows for a visual and interpretable representation of the model's decision-making process. The core idea is that by mapping the neural network's operations into a graph structure, we can gain insights into the feature interactions and pathways that contribute to a prediction. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its potential to improve the transparency and trustworthiness of AI systems. This work introduces a systematic method for translating complex model architectures into understandable graph representations, a key step towards achieving truly explainable AI.

title: Recovering linear images of sparse signals from indirect observations
abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze techniques for recovering a linear image $Bx$ of an unknown signal $x$ from indirect noisy observation $ω=Ax+ξ$. It is {\em a priori} known that $x\in \cX$, a given convex compact set, and that $x$ is $s$-sparse---has at most $s$ nonvanishing entries. The proposed estimates belong to a large family of recovery routines by $\ell_1$-minimization. However, unlike the classical result describing performance of such estimates, we do not make any special (and hard to check) assumptions about the sensing matrix $A$ such as nullspace or Restricted Isometry condition and the like. evidence.abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze techniques for recovering a linear image $Bx$ of an unknown signal $x$ from indirect noisy observation $ω=Ax+ξ$. It is {\em a priori} known that $x\in \cX$, a given convex compact set, and that $x$ is $s$-sparse---has at most $s$ nonvanishing entries. title: Reducing quantum and classical resources for quantum-centric supercomputing workloads on near-term hardware
abstract: Sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SKQD) is a paradigmatic example of a quantum-centric supercomputing workflow that combines the convergence structure of Krylov quantum diagonalization with classical sampling-based post-processing. It provides convergence guarantees assuming that the important computational-basis configurations can be sampled from a set of Krylov states with sufficient probability. We analyze this assumption under depolarizing noise, deriving shot-count resource estimates that expose an exponential depth penalty, and perform experiments on current noisy hardware with the one-dimensional single-impurity Anderson model on a 20-site (40-qubit) instance. Device noise breaks the practical convergence predicted by the noiseless SKQD analysis, but approximate compilation techniques can compress the Krylov time-evolution circuits before execution. The compressed circuits accumulate less hardware noise, recover the expected energy convergence, and reduce both the quantum shot budget and the classical subspace dimension, remaining beneficial even when classical configuration recovery is applied.

title: From Training Data to Patent Thickets: Generative AI, Patent Concentration and Competition in the AI Economy
abstract: Patent filing in generative artificial intelligence has moved from a niche activity to one of the fastest-growing segments of the global patent system. The World Intellectual Property Organisation's 2026 update records that published generative-AI patent families rose from roughly 14,000 in 2023 to over 37,800 in 2025, with more than 56,000 families published across 2024 and 2025 combined, a volume exceeding the entire preceding decade. Ownership is concentrated: China accounts for the largest share, SoftBank has become the single largest corporate holder with almost 3,000 families, and a small set of conglomerates dominate the remaining top ranks. This concentration, layered onto an already dense set of overlapping claims on model architectures, training methods and specialised hardware, has revived a long-standing competition-law concern: the patent thicket. The April 2026 launch of the Shared AI License (SAIL) Foundation by Anthropic, IBM, Meta, Microsoft and Genentech, pooling more than 33,000 patent families, is the clearest institutional response to date, but its scope is narrower and its internal distribution of bargaining power more skewed than the coverage it has received suggests. This paper examines whether Indian law is equipped to respond. It reviews the Patents Act 1970 and the Competition Act 2002, situates them against the compulsory-licensing, FRAND and essential-facilities doctrines developed in the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom and China, and incorporates CCI's October 2025 market study on AI and the Supreme Court's September 2025 order in the Ericsson/Monsanto litigation, which narrowed rather than expanded the Commission's jurisdiction over patent-licensing conduct. The paper argues that India's principal statutory tool against patent aggregation, the compulsory licence under Chapter XVI of the Patents Act, is structurally unsuited to a thicket problem, and that competition-law intervention is now a weaker prospect than earlier commentary assumed. It closes with a set of remedies assessed on their actual, rather than assumed, capacity to work.

title: Graph Neural Network-Based Complex Network Topology Learning
abstract: Complex network topology learning aims to understand the intricate relationships within complex networks, a task critical for diverse applications ranging from social network analysis to biological systems modeling. Traditional approaches often struggle to capture the global structure of these networks, limiting their predictive power and classification accuracy. This paper introduces a novel method leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to effectively learn complex network topologies. The core idea is to utilize the inherent graph structure to learn global topological features and then employ these features for network classification and prediction. We propose a GNN architecture designed to propagate information across the network, allowing each node to aggregate information from its neighbors, ultimately capturing the global context. Our method demonstrates improved performance compared to existing techniques, highlighting the importance of global topology understanding in complex network analysis. The key contributions of this work lie in the development of a robust GNN framework specifically tailored for complex network topology learning, offering a new perspective for understanding and utilizing network structure.

title: Cognitive Graph Construction from Multi-Modal Data Streams
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to graph construction that leverages cognitive principles to create more robust and interpretable representations of the world. Traditional graph construction methods often rely solely on statistical correlations within data, neglecting the underlying cognitive processes that drive human understanding. We introduce an algorithm designed to iteratively build a graph from multi-modal data streams, mimicking how humans construct mental models. This approach prioritizes connections based on coherence and relevance, incorporating mechanisms for handling uncertainty and integrating diverse sensory inputs. The core of the method lies in an iterative process where nodes represent entities, and edges represent relationships between them, dynamically refined as more data becomes available. We define the key mathematical components of this process, including a coherence score and a relevance weighting function. This research contributes to the growing field of knowledge representation and reasoning by providing a framework for building graphs that are not only statistically accurate but also reflect a cognitive understanding of the data. The system demonstrates improved accuracy and interpretability compared to purely data-driven methods.

title: Emma AI - A Humanoid Interactive AI Assistant
abstract: The project presents a prototype of a humanoid, interactive AI assistant called Emma AI, aiming to transcend traditional interaction methods limited to text-based conversations or direct voice responses by combining voice interaction with dynamic visual interaction. The project's core concept is to build an assistant capable of understanding and responding to user requests verbally, while simultaneously controlling the on-screen graphic elements, determining their type and timing based on the nature of the request. The project stems from the need to develop a system that doesn't rely solely on a linguistic model to manage its functions, but rather on a multi-layered architecture that separates inference from operational functions. The system incorporates the Qwen 2.5 7B model, memory management and summarization, web search using Exa, and voice authentication. Its significance lies in providing a practical model for more natural, interconnected, and scalable interaction. Keywords: artificial intelligence, client, Python, voice commands, prediction, engine, logic engine, digital agent, tools, memory, knowledge base, context, voice-to-text, text-to-voice.

title: Geometric Topology of Adaptive Model Search
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for adaptive model search within geometric topology, aiming to improve the estimation of model parameters through automated parameter adjustment guided by geometric structure. The core mechanism centers around constructing an abstract model representing parameter space and iteratively optimizing this model using a self-adjusting process. The paper details the algorithm's design, provides a theoretical analysis of its effectiveness, and presents initial experimental results demonstrating its superior performance compared to existing methods. The focus is on leveraging geometric topology for a more robust and efficient parameter estimation process.

title: Self-Organizing Network Learning: A Quantum Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organizing network learning model based on quantum hybridization. Leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement and superposition, we propose a framework for automatically learning and optimizing complex network structures. The core mechanism involves transforming network nodes and edges into quantum states, utilizing entanglement to facilitate self-organization and optimization. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm compared to traditional network learning techniques, potentially leading to more robust and adaptable learning algorithms. We discuss the theoretical foundations, experimental validation, and potential applications of this quantum-enhanced network learning model.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic neural network structure optimization algorithm, termed "Adaptive Dynamic Neural Network Optimization" (ADN). ADN distinguishes itself through the implementation of a dynamic neural network architecture that automatically adjusts network parameters based on performance feedback. The core mechanism of ADN involves a layered approach, starting with a preliminary network configuration and iteratively refining it through a feedback loop, leveraging the inherent properties of dynamic neural networks to improve model accuracy and generalization. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing neural networks across a range of benchmark datasets. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for advancing neural network design and engineering.

The paper presents a conceptual outline, detailing the design process and potential applications. We argue that this approach presents a significant advancement in computational modeling, potentially unlocking new capabilities within the field of quantum information processing.

title: Formal Model of Trust in Federated Learning Systems
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing. However, the inherent trust relationships within FL systems are complex and often overlooked. This paper presents a formal model for analyzing trust dynamics in FL, incorporating uncertainties in data and model updates. We leverage game theory and Bayesian networks to represent the interactions between participants, considering factors such as data quality, model accuracy, and communication security. The model allows us to formally quantify trust levels and explore strategies for building robust and reliable FL systems. The key contributions of this work lie in providing a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding trust in FL, which can be used to design mechanisms for incentivizing participation, mitigating malicious behavior, and ultimately, enhancing the overall performance and security of FL systems. The model incorporates probabilistic elements represented through conditional probability tables and utility functions, allowing for a nuanced assessment of trust based on various contributing factors. ---

title: Algorithmic Complexity for Parallel Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, but the design and implementation of quantum circuits remain a significant challenge. Traditional approaches often struggle with high fidelity and lengthy circuit construction times, limiting the scalability of quantum computations. This paper introduces a novel algorithmic approach, the "Prioritized Connectivity and Redundancy Minimization" (PCRM) method, designed to address these limitations. We demonstrate its effectiveness in designing parallel quantum circuits, emphasizing circuit connectivity and redundancy reduction, thereby significantly improving fidelity and computational efficiency. The method incorporates a dynamic optimization process that iteratively refines circuit layouts to achieve optimal performance. This research explores the impact of PCRM on various quantum circuit designs, providing a practical framework for accelerating quantum algorithm development.

title: Title: Dynamic Regularization for High-Dimensional Data Distributions
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic regularization method designed to address the challenges posed by high-dimensional data distributions. Traditional regularization techniques often struggle to effectively handle the complex patterns inherent in high-dimensional data, resulting in suboptimal model performance. Our approach leverages the inherent dynamics of high-dimensional data to iteratively adjust regularization parameters, optimizing the data distribution and ultimately enhancing model generalization capabilities. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic parameter adjustment process that mimics the iterative refinement of a process where the regularization strength is constantly adjusted. This iterative refinement is crucial for effectively navigating the intricate landscape of high-dimensional data. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through rigorous analysis and comparison with state-of-the-art techniques, showcasing its ability to improve model performance and generalization across a range of datasets. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed method, highlighting its advantages in terms of robustness and adaptability to diverse data characteristics.

title: Diamond Agent: Agentic Control of Federated HPC Resources as a Service
abstract: Efficiently aggregating and orchestrating computing power across heterogeneous clusters for HPC workflows faces four practical challenges: preserving workflow context across independently administered clusters, moving large datasets between sites, reasoning about site-specific environments and scheduler policies, and exploiting live queue and resource states for efficient task scheduling. To this end, we design Diamond Agent, an agentic system that enables intelligent execution of HPC workflows across heterogeneous clusters with typed skills as the interface. Diamond Agent provides an agent-facing workspace and skills that unify cross-site resource discovery, resource specification, data movement, task execution, and result retrieval. A centralized Diamond Agent instance can operate multiple supercomputers without being deployed separately on each login node. Diamond Agent translates high-level agent actions into valid site-specific executions, moves data through Globus Transfer, and uses live system capability and queue information to select feasible placements. Its event-driven continuation mechanism decouples agent actions from long-running batch jobs: persistent services monitor remote execution and resume the agent only when a result or decision-relevant event is available. evidence.abstract: Efficiently aggregating and orchestrating computing power across heterogeneous clusters for HPC workflows faces four practical challenges: preserving workflow context across independently administered clusters, moving large datasets between sites, reasoning about site-specific environments and scheduler policies, and exploiting live queue and resource states for efficient task scheduling. title: Solving versus Verifying: Catching Contradictions in Tax Reasoning Systems
abstract: Large language models now compute correct tax liabilities on over 90% of well-formed cases in statutory benchmarks, which makes them candidates for the tax-advisory and compliance systems that consume such an answer directly. Real legal inputs, however, are frequently defective: required facts are missing, or stated facts contradict one another. Accuracy on clean benchmarks says nothing about how a model behaves then, and a system that computes straight through a defective input returns a confident number with no sign that anything is wrong. This raises two questions: does a model asked to solve a case abstain when the input is defective, and when it does not, can the same model catch the defect when asked instead to verify the input? We study six recent models on SARA-derived tax cases under missing-fact and contradictory-fact perturbations. The strongest models abstain when a fact is missing but compute through injected contradictions, returning the clean-input answer 63-76% of the time with no signal of the conflict; asked instead to verify the same input, they flag most of those contradictions. We wire that verification call into a simple contradiction gate: one extra call that abstains when the model reports a conflict. Across all six models it recovers most of the missed contradiction abstention at a clean-accuracy cost of at most about 5 percentage points, with no training and no external tooling. High accuracy on well-formed inputs is therefore an incomplete measure of reliability, and the detection the solver misses is cheaply recoverable with a single self-check.

title: Formulazione e Criteri di Falsificazione di un'Ipotesi Predittiva sulla Percezione Consensuale Globale dell'Intelligenza Artificiale Generale (AGI) entro Ottobre 2027
abstract: Autore: Luigi Usai (ORCID: 0009-0003-3001-717X) Ambito Disciplinare: Epistemologia Sperimentale, Computer Science, Econometria dei Sistemi Tecnologici, Technological Forecasting Abstract Il presente lavoro definisce un protocollo predittivo formalmente falsificabile, conforme al criterio di demarcazione popperiano, per determinare l'avvenuto conseguimento dell'Intelligenza Artificiale Generale (AGI) entro e non oltre le ore 23:59 UTC del 31 ottobre 2027. Superando i limiti ontologici ed epistemici legati alla percezione indifferenziata dell'opinione pubblica, il protocollo vincola la transizione di stato a un indice composito ortogonale costituito da tre vettori empirici indipendenti: Consenso quantificato tramite metodo Delphi su un panel qualificato di esperti accademici e industriali; Indicatori econometrici e prestazionali ad alto impatto (macroeconomia del lavoro, testing di autonomia cognitiva, disclosure societaria); Probabilità aggregate sui mercati predittivi ad alta liquidità informazionale. Vengono fissati a priori i livelli di confidenza statistica, i pesi ponderati e le condizioni al contorno sufficienti e necessarie per la confutazione definitiva dell'ipotesi sperimentale. 1. Quadro Epistemologico e Definizione Operativa Ai sensi dell'epistemologia popperiana, un enunciato è scientifico se e solo se la classe dei suoi falsificatori potenziali non è vuota (F=∅). La definizione standard di AGI soffre frequentemente di elasticità tautologica post-hoc (moving the goalposts). Per impedire tale degenerazione protettiva, l'ipotesi assegna valore binario alla proposizione: Θ∈{0,1} dove Θ=1 indica l'avvenuto conseguimento dell'AGI all'interno del dominio reale, verificabile attraverso l'attivazione simultanea o ponderata di grandezze fisiche, contrattuali e computazionali misurabili. 2. Formalizzazione delle Ipotesi Sia IAGI(t)∈[0,1] l'Indice Composito di Transizione Epistemica calcolato alla coordinata temporale t∗=31 Ottobre 2027, ore 23:59 UTC. Ipotesi Sperimentale (H1): IAGI(t∗)≥0,70 Ipotesi Nulla (H0): IAGI(t∗)<0,70 L'indice IAGI è formulato come combinazione convessa di tre sub-indici ortogonali: IAGI=w1ΦExpert+w2ΩProxy+w3ΨMarket con vincolo di normalizzazione sui coefficienti di ponderazione: i=1∑3wi=1con w1=0,35,w2=0,40,w3=0,25 3. Struttura dei Vettori di Rilevazione 3.1. Vettore ΦExpert: Consenso Qualificato (Metodo Delphi Standardizzato) La misurazione esclude la popolazione non specializzata per neutralizzare distorsioni cognitive da marketing e allucinazione euristica. Campionamento: Panel probabilistico (n≥1.000) estratto dalla comunità scientifica attiva: Autori con indice di Hirsch h≥15 in sedi censite (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, IJCAI, ACL, IEEE TPAMI); Chief Technology Officer (CTO) o VP of AI Research di organizzazioni con capitalizzazione/computato primario nel training di frontier models. Quesito Operativo: "I modelli attualmente distribuiti operano con generalizzazione out-of-distribution autonoma equivalente o superiore a un laureato medio nella totalità delle attività cognitive formalizzabili?" Metrica: ΦExpert=NTotale ValidoNAffermativo ΦExpert=1 se ΦExpert≥0,60; altrimenti scalato linearmente su base normalizzata. 3.2. Vettore ΩProxy: Indicatori Comportamentali e Macroeconomici Il sub-indice è una media booleana di tre grandezze macro-osservabili entro t∗: ΩProxy=31(λLabor+λTest+λCorp) Autonomia nel Mercato del Lavoro (λLabor∈{0,1}): Superamento del 15% di linee di codice scritte, verificate, mandate in produzione ed eseguite in ambienti enterprise OCSE senza revisione né commit umano intermediario (dati aggregati da piattaforme di versioning quali GitHub Enterprise, GitLab Enterprise e metriche di audit DORA). Generalizzazione Funzionale e Licenze Professionali (λTest∈{0,1}): Un singolo modello o sistema integrato identico (stessi pesi, nessun fine-tuning settoriale segregato) supera con punteggio nel 95∘ percentile gli esami di abilitazione professionale in: Medicina generale (es. USMLE Step 1, 2 e 3 o equivalenti europei/asiatici); Pratica forense (es. Uniform Bar Examination); Ingegneria computazionale/Matematica applicata (es. Putnam Competition o standard Putnam equivalente con score ≥ top 5%). Disclosure Finanziaria Obbligatoria (λCorp∈{0,1}): Almeno il 25% delle aziende quotate nel paniere S&P 500 / STOXX Europe 600 certifica nei rendiconti trimestrali (Form 10-K SEC o documentazione IFRS) la sostituzione integrale di workflow decisionali o analitici di livello medio-superiore con agenti cognitivi autonomi, quantificandone l'impatto sulla produttività marginale. 3.3. Vettore ΨMarket: Aggregazione Bayesiana tramite Mercati Predittivi I mercati di informazione e probabilità sintetizzano segnali bayesiani riducendo il bias reputazionale individuale: Piattaforme di riferimento: Metaculus (domande a risoluzione formale tracciata), Polymarket e Manifold Markets. Condizione di Validità: Mercati con liquidità reale/volume cumulativo ≥$10.000.000 (o N≥10.000 previsori ponderati per score Brier su Metaculus). Calcolo: Media pesata per volume delle quotazioni di chiusura al 31 ottobre 2027 del contratto con quesito: "Has Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) been achieved by or before October 2027?": ΨMarket=k∑vk⋅pk(t∗) dove pk(t∗) è il prezzo implicito di clearing e vk il peso normalizzato del volume del mercato k. 4. Condizioni di Falsificazione Assoluta L'ipotesi sperimentale H1 si considera definitivamente falsificata, senza riserve interpretative o clausole conservative, qualora alla data spartiacque del 31 ottobre 2027 (23:59 UTC) si realizzi anche una sola delle seguenti condizioni necessarie: Mancato Superamento della Soglia Composita: IAGI(t∗)<0,70 Veto Empirico di Autonomia (ΩProxy=0): Qualora nessun indicatore del vettore ΩProxy risulti verificato (λLabor=0, λTest=0, λCorp=0), a prescindere dal valore di ΦExpert e ΨMarket, indicando la presenza di puro disallineamento narrativo/speculativo privo di sostrato fisico ed economico. Scadenza Cronologica Rigida: Nessuna proroga post-ottobre 2027 sarà ammissibile all'interno del medesimo schema di validazione; qualsiasi transizione successiva costituisce evidenza a favore dell'ipotesi nulla per il frame temporale considerato. 5. Dichiarazione di Trasparenza Metodologica Dati e Codice: Gli script per il calcolo dell'indice aggregato e le API di scaricamento per i mercati predittivi e i registri brevettuali/accademici saranno archiviati con commit crittografico immutabile (SHA-256) a corredo del record Zenodo. Conflitto di Interessi: Nessuno. Licenza: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Per questo motivo, ripubblico nuovamente la mia previsione.

title: On Cognitive Architecture-Based Modeling of Autonomous System Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling the behavior of autonomous systems based on cognitive architecture principles. The core claim is that a cognitive architecture-based modeling method can effectively simulate the cognitive processes and decision-making behaviors of autonomous systems. This is achieved by decomposing the autonomous system's cognitive processes into distinct cognitive modules and utilizing a cognitive architecture to govern their interaction and collaboration. The proposed method offers a deeper understanding of autonomous system decision-making compared to traditional approaches. This work focuses on the theoretical framework and outlines a potential implementation strategy, without empirical validation or experimental results. The key contribution lies in the conceptual model and the methodology for representing and simulating the cognitive aspects of autonomous systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Adaptive Encoding (QEA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum communication scheme, Quantum Entanglement Adaptive Encoding (QEA), designed to enhance the reliability of quantum transmission by leveraging the properties of quantum entanglement. QEA utilizes a feedback mechanism between an encoder and a decoder, both linked through a shared entangled state. The encoder dynamically adjusts the encoding strategy – specifically, the strength of the entanglement and the encoding basis – based on real-time assessment of the channel noise and attenuation. This adaptive approach contrasts with traditional fixed-encoding methods, offering improved resilience against noisy quantum channels. The core claim of this work is that through dynamic adjustment, QEA significantly improves quantum communication reliability. The paper outlines the theoretical framework, describes the QEA protocol, and discusses its potential advantages.

title: Adaptive Program Generation Based on Time-Space Flows
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive program generation by leveraging the concept of time-space flows. Traditional program synthesis techniques often struggle with dynamic environments and the need for iterative optimization. Our method utilizes time-space flow analysis to dissect the execution of a program, identifying patterns and bottlenecks within its control flow and state transitions. These patterns are then modeled as time-space flows, which are analyzed to generate adaptive program fragments. These fragments are integrated into the original program, creating an evolutionary process that dynamically adjusts program behavior. The core claim is that by analyzing the execution of a program as a time-space flow, we can generate programs that are capable of self-optimization. The key mechanism involves a time-space flow network that tracks the evolution of program execution, identifying critical elements for adaptive refinement. This approach differs significantly from static program generation methods, providing a dynamic framework for program optimization and adaptation. The presented system offers the potential to create more robust and efficient programs, particularly in scenarios where the operational environment is unpredictable or subject to change. The theoretical underpinnings and the core algorithm are outlined, demonstrating the feasibility and potential impact of this methodology. ---

title: 基于认知图谱的知识推理系统
abstract: This paper proposes a knowledge reasoning system based on knowledge graphs (KGs). The core claim is to leverage the inherent structure and functionality of KGs to facilitate knowledge reasoning and discovery, ultimately enhancing the intelligence of knowledge systems. The core mechanism involves constructing a system that utilizes graph reasoning algorithms to infer and extract knowledge from the KG. Traditional knowledge reasoning systems heavily rely on manually crafted rules and rule engines, often lacking the automation provided by the structured nature of KGs. This research addresses this limitation by employing KG-specific reasoning techniques. The system presented herein demonstrates the potential for automated knowledge discovery and inference, offering a more scalable and adaptable approach compared to rule-based systems. The system's architecture and reasoning process are detailed, highlighting the integration of KG structure and algorithmic inference. Future work will explore the system's scalability and performance with larger, more complex KGs, as well as investigate novel reasoning algorithms optimized for KG environments.

title: Relational Neural Networks for Structured Data with Temporal Dependencies
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Relational Neural Networks (RNNs) to structured data exhibiting temporal dependencies. Traditional RNNs struggle to effectively represent complex relationships inherent in data where nodes are connected not just by proximity but also by defined interactions. We propose a novel architecture that combines RNNs with Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to address this challenge. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both models: RNNs for capturing temporal dynamics and GCNs for encoding structural relationships. This hybrid approach allows the model to learn both the node connections *and* the temporal evolution associated with those connections. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in capturing intricate patterns within structured data with temporal dependencies. The resulting model achieves improved performance compared to standard RNNs and GCNs when applied to datasets containing both structural and temporal information. The key innovation lies in the unified framework, providing a more comprehensive representation of the data.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Temporal Recurrence and Error Propagation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for neural networks – Self-Correcting Neural Networks (SCNNs) – designed to enhance accuracy and robustness through a mechanism of self-correction. The core concept revolves around incorporating temporal recurrence and error propagation within the network's structure. Specifically, recurrent connections are introduced between layers, facilitating backward flow of information in time. abstract: Quantum-enhanced neural networks (QNNs) represent a promising area of research aiming to surpass classical neural networks in complex pattern recognition tasks. This paper explores a novel QNN architecture utilizing quantum properties like superposition and entanglement to improve learning capabilities. We present a detailed design of this architecture, outlining the key quantum gates and their integration into the network's structure. The core claim is that incorporating these quantum elements will significantly enhance the network's ability to model intricate relationships within data, leading to improved performance in tasks requiring complex pattern detection.

title: Core Claim: Develop a self-adaptive Bayesian network structure optimization algorithm that dynamically adjusts the Bayesian network structure based on data features and model parameters, thereby improving model prediction accuracy and generalization ability.
abstract: This paper investigates a novel self-adaptive Bayesian network structure optimization algorithm designed to enhance model prediction accuracy and generalization ability. Traditional Bayesian network models often struggle to adapt to evolving data patterns. Our approach addresses this limitation by dynamically adjusting the network structure in response to data characteristics and model parameters, resulting in improved performance. We present a new methodology incorporating a dynamic layer adjustment strategy, mitigating the weaknesses of static network designs. The algorithm's effectiveness is validated through a series of experiments utilizing synthetic and real-world datasets. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in both prediction accuracy and generalization across various benchmark scenarios. This work contributes to a more robust and adaptable Bayesian network framework, suitable for a wider range of applications.

title: Semantic Memory Networks with Contextualized Episodic Recall
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for memory networks, termed Semantic Memory Networks with Contextualized Episodic Recall (SMN-CER). The core challenge in current memory networks lies in their inability to effectively integrate and utilize contextual information during episodic recall, limiting their capacity for complex reasoning and understanding. Our approach addresses this by constructing a hierarchical Semantic Memory Network (SMN) that represents semantic knowledge, and then integrating contextualized episodic recall through dynamic weighting. This weighting mechanism adjusts the influence of individual episodic memories based on their relevance to the current context, effectively bridging the gap between semantic and episodic representations. The proposed SMN-CER framework significantly improves recall accuracy and, more importantly, demonstrates enhanced reasoning capabilities by leveraging contextual cues. We argue that this combination represents a fundamental advance in memory network architecture, paving the way for more intelligent and adaptable cognitive models. The key innovation lies in the dynamic contextual weighting, allowing the network to prioritize relevant memories and filter out irrelevant ones during recall. This results in a more focused and accurate retrieval process.

title: 基于神经元网络的自适应时空建模
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to biological system modeling based on neural network architectures and an adaptive spacetime framework. We propose a model that represents biological systems as a network of interconnected "time-space nodes," dynamically adjusting the network's internal parameters to simulate complex dynamic behavior. The core mechanism centers around the utilization of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) within the neural network structure to achieve a level of temporal and spatial complexity surpassing traditional approaches. This work addresses the limitations of existing time-space models by providing a more sophisticated framework for understanding and predicting biological processes. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the model's capacity to generate plausible, albeit simplified, representations of biological time-space dynamics. The study explores the potential for this approach to offer insights into complex biological phenomena.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Algorithms for Graph Traversal and Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum walk algorithms to graph traversal and optimization problems. Classical graph algorithms often struggle with scalability and efficiency when dealing with large and complex graphs. Quantum walks, utilizing the principles of superposition and interference, offer a potential solution by providing a fundamentally different approach to graph exploration. We present a framework for constructing quantum walk-based algorithms tailored for graph traversal, focusing on algorithms that can efficiently explore the graph space. Furthermore, we explore the integration of these algorithms into graph optimization problems, aiming to achieve speedups compared to traditional classical methods. The core idea is to represent graph nodes and edges as quantum states, enabling parallel exploration of the graph through quantum superposition. We explore the mathematical formulation of these algorithms, highlighting key concepts like Hilbert space representation, transition amplitudes, and interference effects. The results presented demonstrate the potential for quantum walk algorithms to significantly improve the performance of graph-related tasks.

title: Formal Verification of Differential Privacy Mechanisms
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to verifying the differential privacy guarantees of complex algorithms. Traditional methods rely heavily on empirical analysis, which can be susceptible to errors and may not fully capture the intricacies of algorithm execution. We introduce a formal verification framework leveraging model checking and abstract interpretation to rigorously prove the privacy loss bounds. The framework allows for a detailed analysis of algorithm states and transitions, ensuring that the privacy budget is never exceeded. This work addresses a critical gap in the practical deployment of differential privacy mechanisms by providing a robust and verifiable method for guaranteeing privacy. The core contribution lies in the combination of these techniques, offering a scalable and reliable solution for complex privacy-preserving systems. We define the key variables and operations used within the framework, providing a clear mathematical foundation for the verification process. Specifically, we use the following notation: *x* represents a data point, *k* represents the number of queries made to the algorithm, *ε* represents the privacy parameter, *δ* represents the failure probability, *L(f)* represents the loss function of a function *f*, *μ* represents the support of the data distribution, and *Δ* represents the difference between two states in the model. The framework systematically tracks the cumulative privacy loss, ensuring adherence to the desired *ε* and *δ* constraints.

title: Evolutionary Algorithms for Compiler Optimization – Genetic Programming with Graph Transformations
abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms, specifically genetic programming (GP), to the domain of compiler optimization. The core argument presented is that GP offers a novel and potentially powerful method for generating highly optimized compiler code by directly manipulating control flow graphs. Traditional compiler optimization relies heavily on manually designed heuristics, which can be complex to develop, maintain, and often fail to achieve optimal results across diverse codebases. This research proposes a framework where compiler optimizations are represented as genetic programs, allowing for automated exploration of the optimization space. The fitness function is designed to evaluate the performance of the transformed code based on key metrics. We detail the core mechanisms involved, focusing on the representation of optimizations within GP and the process of iteratively evolving these programs to improve code efficiency. The potential benefits of this approach, including increased optimization effectiveness and reduced reliance on manual tuning, are discussed.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Storage: A Novel Non-Classical Quantum Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unprecedented information storage and processing capabilities. Traditional quantum computing approaches often struggle with limited storage density and instability, hindering the development of complex algorithms. This paper explores a novel non-classical quantum algorithm centered around entanglement, aiming to transcend the limitations of classical qubit storage and manipulation. We propose a method leveraging entangled qubit states to perform complex transformations and manipulate quantum information with enhanced fidelity and efficiency. The core claim of this work is that this algorithm represents a significant step towards realizing more efficient and stable quantum information storage and entanglement operations, potentially unlocking new avenues for quantum computation. This research utilizes the unique properties of entangled qubit states to overcome inherent bottlenecks in current quantum computing paradigms. The proposed algorithm offers a fundamentally different approach to data storage and manipulation, potentially revolutionizing the landscape of quantum information processing.

title: 基于自适应的深度学习模型优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to deep learning model optimization, termed "Adaptive Deep Learning Optimization" (ADLO). ADLO leverages dynamic adjustments to both model parameters and optimization algorithms to automate parameter tuning and improve model performance during training. The core mechanism of ADLO involves a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the model's performance and adapts the optimization strategy accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ADLO through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and convergence speed compared to traditional optimization methods. The paper also discusses the limitations of current optimization techniques and outlines future research directions, including exploring more sophisticated adaptive strategies and incorporating uncertainty estimation.

title: AVSplat: Dense-View Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Assist-View Preconditioning
abstract: Pose-free feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting enables novel view synthesis from uncalibrated multi-view images. Although more views should improve performance, existing methods often degrade with dense-view inputs because global aggregation spreads attention over many tokens, and naive voxel fusion averages many Gaussians into overly smooth representations. We present AVSplat, a framework that turns additional views into reliable signals for both aggregation and representation. Before global attention, each view performs a single lightweight interaction with a small set of Assist Views chosen for relevance and diversity, and the cached features provide a focused scene context that stabilizes correspondence. For representation, we use adaptive temperature-aware voxel fusion that sharpens attribution under high occupancy, guided by occupancy and point confidence. Crucially, AVSplat restores positive view scaling where performance remains stable or improves as more input views are added, instead of degrading in the dense-view regime. Ablations show that Assist View Preconditioning is primarily responsible for preventing dense-view degradation, while Occupancy-guided Voxel Fusion contributes most of the single-point image-quality gains.

title: Maslow Detector — Reproducible Linguistic Analysis System
abstract: Maslow Detector is a reproducible rule-based system for analyzing textual signals associated with human needs, Maslow-inspired levels, persuasion techniques, emotional and linguistic signals, and claims that may warrant further verification. The system does not attempt to measure a person's psychological state or determine what a person “really needs”. Maslow's hierarchy is used as an interpretive framework for classifying linguistic signals present in text. The core analysis is performed by a deterministic JavaScript engine based on explicit linguistic patterns, rules, negation handling, contextual analysis, source-related patterns, and transparent heuristics. This release includes: • A self-contained HTML detector: detector_v7_8_signature_lang.html• A Google Chrome Extension V2 (Manifest V3)• A reusable modular analysis engine• Spanish and English language support• Local analysis without network access or external AI services The modular engine was extracted from the reference HTML implementation and verified against a frozen regression baseline of 106 reference cases. The extracted engine produced results identical to the reference implementation in all 106 cases. The same engine is included in the Chrome extension and can also run independently of the browser DOM and browser APIs. The current system provides need-level classification, primary and secondary classifications, ambiguity indicators, contextual and linguistic matching, negation handling, persuasion-related techniques, distinction between used and merely mentioned techniques, source-related analysis, claim verification signals, quote and evidence extraction, and deterministic scoring. This project is a reproducible research and development system. It is not a psychological diagnostic instrument or a validated measurement of human needs. The classifications represent linguistic analysis based on explicit rules and heuristics. False positives and false negatives are possible. The current release performs its core analysis locally. It does not require an Anthropic API key, remote backend, network access, or external AI inference. An expanded-analysis component using a dedicated backend connected to the Anthropic API is currently under development and is planned for a subsequent version. This functionality is not part of the present release. The API key is intended to remain exclusively on the backend. The Chrome extension is functional in a real Chrome environment and is currently being prepared for inclusion in the next version, which is planned to include its Chrome Web Store publication. Future Development The project is designed to allow the future incorporation of additional frameworks for the analysis of human needs, motivation, and persuasion, while preserving the existing deterministic engine and modular architecture. Planned research directions include the exploration of complementary models, including Manfred Max-Neef's Human Needs Matrix, Self-Determination Theory, and other relevant frameworks. These directions form part of the planned evolution of Maslow Detector and are not implemented in the present release. El sistema no pretende medir el estado psicológico de una persona ni determinar qué es lo que una persona “realmente necesita”. La jerarquía de Maslow se utiliza como marco interpretativo para clasificar señales lingüísticas presentes en el texto. El análisis principal se realiza mediante un motor JavaScript determinista basado en patrones lingüísticos explícitos, reglas, tratamiento de negaciones, análisis contextual, patrones relacionados con fuentes y heurísticas transparentes. Desarrollo futuro El proyecto está diseñado para permitir la incorporación futura de otros marcos de análisis de necesidades humanas, motivación y persuasión, manteniendo el motor determinista y la arquitectura modular existentes. Entre las líneas de investigación previstas se contempla la exploración de modelos complementarios, entre ellos la Matriz de Necesidades Humanas de Manfred Max-Neef, la Self-Determination Theory (Teoría de la Autodeterminación) y otros marcos relevantes. En desarrollo. Estas líneas forman parte de la evolución prevista de Maslow Detector y no están implementadas en la presente versión. Esta versión incluye: • Un detector HTML autocontenido: detector_v7_8_signature_lang.html• Una extensión de Google Chrome V2 (Manifest V3)• Un motor de análisis modular reutilizable• Soporte para español e inglés• Análisis local sin acceso a red ni servicios externos de inteligencia artificial El motor modular fue extraído de la implementación HTML de referencia y verificado frente a una línea base de regresión congelada de 106 casos de referencia. El motor extraído produjo resultados idénticos a la implementación de referencia en los 106 casos. El mismo motor está incluido en la extensión de Chrome y también puede ejecutarse independientemente del DOM y de las API del navegador. El sistema actual proporciona clasificación de niveles de necesidad, clasificaciones primaria y secundaria, indicadores de ambigüedad, análisis lingüístico y contextual, tratamiento de negaciones, técnicas relacionadas con la persuasión, distinción entre técnicas utilizadas y simplemente mencionadas, análisis relacionado con fuentes, señales de afirmaciones que pueden requerir verificación, extracción de citas y evidencias, y puntuación determinista. Este proyecto es un sistema reproducible de investigación y desarrollo. No constituye un instrumento de diagnóstico psicológico ni una medición validada de las necesidades humanas. Las clasificaciones representan un análisis lingüístico basado en reglas y heurísticas explícitas. Pueden producirse falsos positivos y falsos negativos. La presente versión realiza el análisis principal localmente. No requiere una clave de API de Anthropic, un backend remoto, acceso a red ni inferencia mediante inteligencia artificial externa. Un componente de ampliación del análisis mediante un backend propio conectado a la API de Anthropic se encuentra actualmente en desarrollo y está previsto para una versión posterior. Esta funcionalidad no forma parte de la presente versión. La clave de API está prevista para permanecer exclusivamente en el backend. La extensión de Chrome es funcional en un entorno real de Chrome y actualmente se está preparando para su inclusión en la próxima versión, en la que está prevista su publicación en Chrome Web Store. title: Decentralized Federated Optimization with Byzantine Fault Tolerance via Blockchain
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, the inherent vulnerability of FL to malicious participants, known as Byzantine attacks, poses a significant threat to the integrity and convergence of the learning process. This paper proposes a novel framework for decentralized federated optimization with Byzantine fault tolerance leveraging blockchain technology. Our approach utilizes a blockchain network to establish a tamper-proof record of model updates, ensuring data integrity and enabling robust aggregation even in the presence of malicious actors. The core mechanism involves a distributed consensus algorithm on the blockchain to validate and aggregate model updates, guaranteeing Byzantine fault tolerance. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, providing a secure and reliable foundation for decentralized FL. The key contributions include a blockchain-based architecture for FL, a Byzantine fault tolerance mechanism, and a system for ensuring model integrity. The proposed system addresses the critical challenge of security in FL, offering a pathway toward trustworthy and resilient distributed learning.

title: Quantum-Inspired Graph Clustering using Amplitude Estimation
abstract: Graph clustering, the process of grouping nodes in a graph based on their relationships, is a cornerstone of numerous data analysis applications, including social network analysis, bioinformatics, and anomaly detection. Traditional graph clustering algorithms often struggle with scalability and computational complexity, particularly when dealing with large graphs. This paper proposes a novel approach to graph clustering that leverages quantum-inspired amplitude estimation techniques. By mimicking the probabilistic nature of quantum algorithms, we approximate the probability distribution of node assignments within clusters, significantly accelerating the clustering process. Our method utilizes a modified version of the Lloyd-Max algorithm, incorporating amplitude estimation to reduce the number of iterations required to converge to a stable clustering solution. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and algorithmic design, that this approach can achieve comparable or superior clustering performance compared to conventional methods, while exhibiting a markedly reduced computational footprint. The core contribution lies in adapting amplitude estimation principles – originally developed for quantum computing – to a classical graph clustering context, offering a potentially transformative solution for tackling computationally intensive graph clustering problems. The efficiency gains are particularly pronounced in scenarios with high-dimensional node feature spaces.

title: Quantum Entanglement Randomness Matrix Generation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity to generate truly random matrices. This paper explores the development of a novel algorithm based on entangled quantum states to create and manipulate random matrices with complex quantum entanglement structures. We introduce a mechanism that leverages the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled systems to generate random matrices, offering a potential pathway to enhance simulation capabilities in quantum computing and information processing. The core claim is that this algorithm can produce matrices with intricate entanglement patterns, providing a more robust and controllable source of randomness than existing methods. The algorithm's novelty lies in its integration of entanglement as a core component of the random matrix generation process. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the algorithm's ability to generate matrices exhibiting specific entanglement properties.

title: 基于量子自适应的拓扑变换算法
abstract: Quantum-inspired topology transformations are a burgeoning field with the potential to revolutionize computational geometry and related tasks. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, termed "Quantum Adaptive Topology Transform" (QATT), leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum computation to dynamically adjust transformation parameters, thereby significantly enhancing the efficiency of topology transformations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QATT through rigorous analysis and practical implementation, highlighting its ability to overcome limitations of traditional approaches. The core mechanism centers around a quantum state evolution process that iteratively refines transformation parameters based on a feedback loop, leading to improved results with minimal computational overhead. This work presents a fundamentally new approach to topology transformations, offering a promising pathway towards more efficient and versatile algorithms.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic parameter adjustment algorithm designed to optimize systems exhibiting dynamic behavior. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often lack adaptability, necessitating a shift towards dynamic adjustments. This research proposes a framework that integrates the system's dynamic evolution with the parameter adjustment process, ensuring the algorithm responds effectively to system changes. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a feedback loop that continuously monitors system state, adjusts parameters based on this feedback, and refines the optimization process. This dynamic adaptation significantly enhances the algorithm's ability to achieve optimal performance in complex, evolving systems. The resulting algorithm provides a robust and adaptable approach to parameter tuning, offering improved performance compared to static methods in scenarios with significant system variability.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization framework leveraging adaptive topology to guide the optimization of quantum systems. Traditional optimization methods often require manual parameter tuning, presenting a challenge in the complex landscape of quantum systems. We propose a method that utilizes the inherent topological properties of the system to simplify the problem space and facilitate the discovery of optimal parameter configurations. The core mechanism centers on adapting the topology structure to the system's specific characteristics, enabling the system to converge to a solution that maximizes performance metrics. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional optimization techniques, particularly for complex quantum systems, and holds the potential for enhanced performance and reduced computational effort.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Data Structures with Adaptive Representation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of novel data structures leveraging non-Euclidean geometry to achieve adaptive representation and enhanced data handling capabilities. Traditional data structures often rely on rigid assumptions about data relationships, limiting their flexibility and efficiency. We propose a new data structure model centered around geometric transformations that dynamically adjust the structure of the data based on its inherent properties. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm for data management, potentially leading to significant improvements in storage, retrieval, and processing efficiency. The core of this research involves the design of a representation that incorporates geometric transformations, enabling the data structure to automatically adapt its structure to best represent the data. This paper explores the theoretical foundations and potential implementation of this new data structure, outlining the key mechanisms and demonstrating preliminary results through illustrative examples. The focus will be on exploring the benefits of this approach in various data scenarios, including scenarios involving dynamic data transformations and data that exhibits complex relationships. We will discuss challenges and future directions for this research, emphasizing the potential for a paradigm shift in data representation and management.

title: Title: Modular Quantum Error Correction with Adaptive Resonance Networks
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary computational capabilities, but the inherent fragility of quantum systems necessitates robust error correction techniques. Traditional error correction codes, while effective, often rely on fixed parameters, limiting scalability and introducing vulnerabilities. This paper proposes a novel modular quantum error correction scheme utilizing Adaptive Resonance Networks (ARNs) to dynamically adjust the error correction rate based on the specific error profile of a quantum system. This approach addresses the instability inherent in current codes, offering a potential pathway toward more robust and scalable error mitigation.
